orientation: Compact typed tokens losslessly encoded all twelve behavioral snapshots and reduced bytes by 64.27% versus prose and 17.22% versus JSON. A one-model exploratory probe scored compact prompts highest, but reused sessions, post hoc design, correlated formats, and backend nondeterminism make that reasoning result hypothesis-generating only.
finding: The compact schema is validated as a lossless, smaller transport for the bounded observations; no reasoning advantage was established.
limitations: The model probe reused twelve sessions with one model and one prompt under a post hoc protocol.
The three representations were correlated and backend repeatability was not guaranteed.
Byte savings did not map directly to token savings because the shared legend dominated prompts.
negative_evidence: Prose and JSON probe accuracy remained near chance, and the compact numerical lead is not confirmatory.
The compact prompt reduced model-counted tokens only slightly relative to JSON.
evidence_quotes: The compact representation was **64.27% smaller than deterministic prose** and **17.22% smaller than canonical JSON**.
JSON and compact decoding both retained exact numerical equality across all 12 snapshots.
The compact representation's numerical lead over chance-level prose and JSON is hypothesis-generating only
Byte reduction also did not translate directly into token reduction.
